title: Humanizer list
description: Phrases and habits that mark product copy as written by a language model, for one language. Matching rules are in src/matcher.mjs.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code of the language, also the folder name and the prefix of every id.

foldDiacritics.description: Whether diacritics are dropped before matching (the tilde of ñ is always kept). Defaults to true. Set to false for a language whose accents tell words apart.

id.description: Unique id: the language code, a hyphen, then kebab-case words.

kind.description: word: one whole word. phrase: whole words, any whitespace between them, … for a short gap. regex: JavaScript regular expression compiled with the flags giu.

match.description: May not start or end with … (a gap needs words on both sides).

precision.description: high: one hit flags a text. medium: counts only with a medium hit from another entry.

evidence.description: What backs the entry. corpus: it fired in independent machine text (model answers or a shared-task corpus). imitation: only in the imitation set written with the list in view. reasoning: in no machine corpus; kept because the form is a clear chat leftover or calque and never fired on human copy.

domain.description: Where the entry is precise. general: within its level's bar on every general human corpus (web pages and news or similar), so it may run on any prose. product: within the bar only on product copy; run it on titles and product descriptions only.

why.description: Why this reads as machine-written, in English.

example.description: A sentence the entry must match.

rewrite.description: The same content as a person would write it. The entry must not match it.

falsePositives.description: Ordinary sentences close to the pattern that it must not match.
